emotions.name: Grief
emotions.definition: Loss-oriented sadness specifically tied to absence — of people, objects, identity, place, or routines that no longer exist.

emotions.name: Fear
emotions.definition: Anticipatory anxiety, dread, hypervigilance, worry about future harm or recurrence.

emotions.name: Anger
emotions.definition: Active, energized opposition. Includes righteous anger at institutions, frustration that mobilizes action.

emotions.name: Weariness
emotions.definition: Exhaustion accumulated over time. Distinct from anger or sadness — flat, depleted, low-energy.

emotions.name: Hope
emotions.definition: Forward-looking positive expectation. Often tied to visible progress, community support, or imagined future states.

emotions.name: Relief
emotions.definition: Reduction of acute pressure. The release-after-tension affect. Often paired with safety, completion, or external help arriving.

emotions.name: Numbness
emotions.definition: Affective absence. Dissociation, detachment, inability to feel. Distinct from weariness — there is *less* affect, not depleted affect.

emotions.name: Resignation
emotions.definition: Acceptance without endorsement. The 'this is just how it is' affect. Distinct from weariness (resignation is cognitive; weariness is somatic) and numbness (resignation feels something — namely, defeat).

emotions.name: Defiance
emotions.definition: Active resistance to defeat or expectation. The 'I refuse' affect. Often coexists with anger but is more identity-claiming.

emotions.name: Gratitude
emotions.definition: Thankfulness directed at people, institutions, or circumstances. Distinct from relief — gratitude is other-directed; relief is self-experienced.

emotions.name: Pride
emotions.definition: Self-directed positive evaluation. Often appears around competence demonstrated under hard circumstances, or community/family members' actions.

emotions.name: Neutral / procedural
emotions.definition: Affectively flat. Procedural, descriptive, factual. Use when the speech is genuinely neutral, not when affect is mixed or unclear.
